discovery: Cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmic structure

nominees.name: Alexei A. Starobinsky
nominees.affiliation: Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, Russian Academy of Sciences, Russia

motivation: Starobinsky (1979-80) and Guth (1981) proposed that the early universe underwent a phase of accelerated expansion, resolving the horizon and flatness problems. Mukhanov (with the late Chibisov, 1981) and Starobinsky showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed all cosmic structure, predicting a nearly scale-invariant, adiabatic, Gaussian spectrum with a small red tilt. These were bold, falsifiable predictions. Over two decades, WMAP and Planck confirmed them with exquisite precision: spatial flatness, coherent acoustic peaks and superhorizon adiabatic correlations, Gaussianity to a part in ten thousand, and a spectral index n_s ≈ 0.965, which excludes exact scale invariance at over eight sigma. Having scrutinised these data systematically, I regard the quantum origin of galaxies as an empirically established result. It connects quantum field theory and gravity to the largest observable scales and has turned the first instants of the universe into a laboratory.
